summary: Evaluate the bounded SI Green response of signed circular filaments at cylindrical R,Z targets.

identity.relation: Circular-filament vector potential and magnetic-field response
identity.direction: source filaments and target points to psi, BR, BZ
identity.definition: psi=R A_phi with per-ampere filament weights
identity.model: Ideal circular filaments with complete elliptic-integral and small-parameter analytic branch
identity.coordinates: R and Z in metres; source rows are radius, height, signed weight
identity.boundary: Axis values are analytic; active ideal-filament coincidence is singular

inputs.name: rzw
inputs.description: Source rows or a list of independent source sets.
inputs.constraints: Non-negative source radius; signed weights; list output preserves set dimension.

outputs.name: response
outputs.description: Tuple psi, BR, BZ; list source input returns one target axis per set.
outputs.units: Wb/rad per ampere; T per ampere

supported: Named finite off-axis and axis-limit fixtures

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for malformed, nonfinite, negative-radius, or coincident active-filament inputs.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises FloatingPointError for overflow, invalid arithmetic, or nonfinite output.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this is a direct kernel.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial result is returned after a failed source evaluation.

provenance.lineage_summary: Derived from the retained Pleiades circular-filament implementation with an explicit bounded successor contract and independent azimuthal quadrature comparison.
provenance.license_status: Retained source lineage and license evidence are available; public release licensing remains pending.

example.description: Evaluate one unit-weight filament at two finite targets.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.electromagnetism import compute_greens
psi, br, bz = compute_greens(np.array([[1.0, 0.0, 1.0]]), np.array([[0.2, 0.3], [0.4, -0.2]]))
assert psi.shape == br.shape == bz.shape == (2,)
example.expected: Three finite arrays with shape (2,) are returned.

verification.evidence_ceiling: Named fixtures and declared API behavior only; no complete scientific correctness or interchangeability claim.
known_limitations: Irregular legacy reflected-block mismatch is preserved and not rebound.
Extreme-scale behavior and finite-wire physics are unqualified.
Human approval and release readiness are not established.
